'''Remo Ruffini''' (born May 17, 1942, [[La Brigue]], [[Alpes-Maritimes]], at that time, Briga Marittima, Italy) is an Italian astrophysicist. He is the Director of [[ICRANet]], International Centre for Relativistic Astrophysics Network and one of the founders of the [[International Center for Relativistic Astrophysics|International Centre for Relativistic Astrophysics]] (ICRA). Ruffini initiated the International Relativistic Astrophysics PhD (IRAP PhD), a common graduate school program of several universities and research institutes for the education of theoretical astrophysicists. He is the Director of the Erasmus Mundus IRAP PhD program (IRAP Ph D Erasmus Mundus). He has been Professor of Theoretical Physics at the [[Sapienza University of Rome|University of Rome "Sapienza"]] from 1978 to 2012.

==Biography==
After obtaining his degree in 1966 in [[Rome]], he was a post-doctoral fellow at the [[Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Literatur|Mainz Academy of Sciences]] working with [[Pascual Jordan]], in [[West Germany]]. Then, he was a post-doctoral fellow with [[John Archibald Wheeler|John Wheeler]] and Member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in Princeton and later became an instructor and assistant professor at [[Princeton University]]. In 1975, he was a visiting professor at the Universities of Kyoto (Japan) and of Western Australia, Perth. In the years 1975–78, he worked with NASA, being a member of the task force on the scientific use of space stations. In 1976 he became professor of theoretical physics at the [[University of Catania]] and in 1978 he was appointed a professor at the [[Sapienza University of Rome|University "Sapienza"]]. In 1985, he was elected president of the [[International Center for Relativistic Astrophysics]] (ICRA). In 1984 he was a cofounder, with [[Abdus Salam]], of the Marcel Grossmann Meetings.<ref>Alex Gaina, MARCEL GROSSMANN MEETING-AN IMPORTANT EVENT IN GRAVITATION AND ASTROPHYSICS [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332381243_Mesto_dla_formuly1_MARCEL_GROSSMANN_MEEETING-AN_IMPORTANT_EVENT_IN_GRAVITATION_AND_ASTROPHYSICS/figures ]</ref> In 1987, he became co-chairman of the Italian-Korean Meetings on Relativistic Astrophysics. In the years 1989–93, he was President of the Scientific Committee of the [[Italian Space Agency]]. He is the editor of a variety of scientific journals. He is married to Anna Imponente and has a son, Iacopo.

His theoretical work led to the concept of [[Exotic star#Boson stars|boson stars]].<ref>
{{cite journal
|author1=R. Ruffini  |author2=S. Bonazzola
 |name-list-style=amp | year = 1969
| title = Systems of Self-Gravitating Particles in General Relativity and the Concept of an Equation of State
| journal = [[Physical Review]]
| volume = 187 | issue = 5 | pages = 1767–1783
| doi =  10.1103/PhysRev.187.1767
|bibcode = 1969PhRv..187.1767R |hdl=2060/19690028071
 | hdl-access = free}}</ref> His classic  article with [[John Archibald Wheeler|John Wheeler]]<ref>
{{cite journal
|author1=R. Ruffini  |author2=J.A. Wheeler
 |name-list-style=amp | year = 1971
| title = Introducing the Black Hole
| journal = [[Physics Today]]
| volume= 24|issue= 1| pages = 30–41
| doi=10.1063/1.3022513 
|bibcode = 1971PhT....24a..30R | doi-access= free}}</ref> popularized the astrophysical concept of [[Black Hole]].<ref>[https://www.worldwidewords.org/topicalwords/tw-bla1.htm Naming of black hole].</ref> With [[Demetrios Christodoulou]] he has given the formula for a [[Kerr–Newman metric|Kerr-Newmann Black Hole]] endowed of charge, mass and angular momentum.<ref>
{{cite journal
|author1=D. Christodoulou |author2=R. Ruffini | year = 1971
| title = Reversible Transformations of a Charged Black Hole
| journal = [[Physical Review D]]
| volume = 4 | issue = 12 | pages = 3552–3555
| doi =  10.1103/PhysRevD.4.3552
|bibcode = 1971PhRvD...4.3552C }}</ref> His theoretical work led to the identification of the first [[Black hole|Black Holes]] in the [[Milky Way|Milky Way Galaxy]].

Together with his student C. Rhoades,<ref>
{{cite journal
|author1=C. Rhoades  |author2=R. Ruffini
 |name-list-style=amp | year = 1974
| title = Maximum Mass of a Neutron Star
| journal = [[Physical Review Letters]]
| volume = 32 |issue= 6| pages = 324
| doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.32.324
| bibcode=1974PhRvL..32..324R
}}</ref> he established the absolute upper limit to the mass of [[neutron star]]s. With his student Robert Leach,<ref>
{{cite journal
|author1=R. Leach  |author2=R. Ruffini
 |name-list-style=amp | year = 1973
| title = On the Masses of X-Ray Sources
| journal = [[Astrophysical Journal Letters]]
| volume = 180 | pages = L15
| doi = 10.1086/181143
| bibcode=1973ApJ...180L..15L
}}</ref> he used such an upper limit for fixing the paradigm which enabled the identification of the first Black Hole in the Milky Way Galaxy, [[Cygnus X1]], using the splendid data of the [[Uhuru (satellite)|Uhuru satellite]] by [[Riccardo Giacconi]] and his group.<ref>
{{cite journal
| author = R. Giacconi
| year = 2005
| title = An Education in Astronomy
| journal = [[Annual Review of Astronomy & Astrophysics]]
| volume = 43 | issue = 1 | pages = 1–30
| doi = 10.1146/annurev.astro.43.090303.091253
| bibcode=2005ARA&A..43....1G
| doi-access = free
}}</ref><ref>
{{cite journal
| author = R. Giacconi
| year = 2003
| title = Nobel Lecture: The dawn of x-ray astronomy
| journal = [[Reviews of Modern Physics]]
| volume = 75 | issue = 3| pages = 995–1010
| doi = 10.1103/RevModPhys.75.995
| bibcode=2003RvMP...75..995G
| doi-access = free
}}</ref>

For these works, Ruffini won the [[Abraham Cressy Morrison|A. Cressy Morrison]] Award of the [[New York Academy of Sciences]] in 1972.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Ruffini|first=Remo|date=1973|title=Neutron Stars and Black Holes in Our Galaxy*|url=https://nyaspubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.2164-0947.1973.tb01960.x|journal=Transactions of the New York Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=35|issue=3 Series II|pages=196–226|doi=10.1111/j.2164-0947.1973.tb01960.x|issn=2164-0947|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

With his students [[Daniela Calzetti|Calzetti]], Giavalisco, Song and Taraglio, Ruffini developed the role of fractal structures in cosmology.<ref>
{{cite journal
|author1=D. Calzetti|author1-link= Daniela Calzetti |author2=M. Giavalisco |author3=R. Ruffini | year = 1988
| title = The normalization of the correlation functions for extragalactic structures
| journal = [[Astronomy and Astrophysics]]
| volume = 198 |issue= 1–2|pages=1
|bibcode=1988A&A...198....1C }}</ref><ref>
{{cite journal
|author1=R. Ruffini |author2=D.J. Song |author3=S. Taraglio | year = 1988
| title = The 'ino' mass and the cellular large-scale structure of the universe
| journal = [[Astronomy and Astrophysics]]
| volume = 190 |issue= 1–2|pages=1
|bibcode=1988A&A...190....1R }}</ref>

Together with his collaborator [[Thibault Damour]],<ref>
{{cite journal
|author1=T. Damour  |author2=R. Ruffini
 |name-list-style=amp | year = 1975
| title = Quantum Electrodynamical Effects in Kerr-Newmann Geometries
| journal = [[Physical Review Letters]]
| volume = 35 | issue = 7 | page = 463
| doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.35.463
| bibcode=1975PhRvL..35..463D
}}</ref> Ruffini suggested the applicability of the Heisenberg-Euler-Schwinger process of pair creation in black hole physics and identified the [[dyadosphere]] where these processes take place. [[Gamma ray burst]]s seem to give the observational evidence of such pair creation process in astrophysics, prior to the observation of such phenomenon in Earth based experiments and represent the first evidence of the energy extraction process from Black Holes (the blackholic energy).<ref>
{{cite conference
| author = R. Ruffini| year = 2008
| title = Gamma Ray Bursts
| book-title = Proceedings XI Marcel Grossmann Meeting
| publisher = [[World Scientific]]
|display-authors=etal}}</ref>

==Books==
He is co-author of 21 books, including:
*[[Riccardo Giacconi|R. Giacconi]] and R. Ruffini, ''Physics and Astrophysics of Neutron Stars and Black Holes'', LXXV E. Fermi Summer School, SIF and North Holland (1978); also translated into Russian
*[[Riccardo Giacconi|R. Giacconi]] and R. Ruffini, ''Physics and Astrophysics of Neutron Stars and Black Holes'' 2nd edition, Cambridge Scientific Publishers, Cambridge (2009)
*R. Gursky and R. Ruffini, ''Neutron Stars, Black Holes and Binary X Ray Sources'', H. Reidel (1975)
*H. Ohanian and R. Ruffini. [https://books.google.com/books/about/Gravitation_and_Spacetime.html?id=5DtkqcET4b0C ''Gravitation and Spacetime''], W.W. Norton (1994); translated into Italian (Bologna: Zanichelli, 1997), Chinese (China Science Publishing, 2007) and Korean (Seoul: Shin Won, 2001)
*[[James M. Bardeen|Bardeen]], et al., ''Black Holes'', Gordon & Breach (1973)
*[[Martin Rees, Baron Rees of Ludlow|M. Rees]], [[John Archibald Wheeler|J.A. Wheeler]] and R. Ruffini, ''Black Holes, Gravitational Waves and Cosmology'', Gordon & Breach (1974)
*H. Sato and R. Ruffini, ''Black Holes'', Tokyo (1976)
*[[Fang Lizhi|L.Z. Fang]] and R. Ruffini, ''Basic Concepts in Relativistic Astrophysics'', Beijing: Science Press (1981)
*F. Melchiorri and R. Ruffini, ''Gamow Cosmology'', North Holland Pub. Co., (1986)
